claims.statement: The dbt package is Jinja-only and uses stock dbt-postgres; its PostgreSQL stream_table materialization translates compiled model SQL into extension SQL API calls rather than implementing a Python adapter.
The package manifest permits dbt >=1.9.0,<2.0.0, while the integration runner defaults to dbt Core and dbt-postgres 1.10 in a dedicated .venv-dbt.

The materialization derives its reported table relation from this, separately constructs the API target using stream_table_schema/name overrides, and currently defaults to schedule 1m, refresh mode AUTO, and initialize true.
Stream-table existence is checked in pgt_stream_tables rather than solely dbt's cache, before pre-hooks; the helper handles a two-part name by splitting on dots and otherwise uses target.schema.
Full refresh uses should_full_refresh(), commits a drop for an existing stream table and then uses ordinary create, bypassing create-or-replace even when available.

Create-or-replace capability detection probes pg_proc and pg_namespace for a function name and caches the boolean in the dbt context; it does not validate the function signature or all option compatibility.

Ordinary runs use create-or-replace when available; the server creates absent tables and compares rewritten, whitespace-normalized queries and configuration for existing tables before no-op or delegation to alter.
The current fallback path alters changed defining queries in place using the query parameter rather than dropping and recreating them, contrary to older package guidance.

Status and fuse settings are applied separately via metadata lookup and alter; first ordinary create applies configured status, whereas first create-or-replace with status alone skips this follow-up unless the table previously existed or a fuse setting is supplied.

The alter wrapper skips work without metadata and sends NULL for unchanged compared fields, but any non-null append_only or differential threshold option forces needs_alter; the materialization passes append_only=false by default.

The materialization executes main SELECT 1, runs post-hooks, and returns the relation derived from this without an explicit cache_new call or rebuilding the relation for stream-table naming overrides.
All mutating adapter macros use statement blocks with auto_begin=False and fetch_result=False around explicit BEGIN/COMMIT; run_query is not an independent DDL connection or commit boundary.
Lifecycle mutations are not atomic with the whole dbt model: committed drops, creates, and alters cannot be undone by failure in a later lifecycle step or post-hook.

String-valued API and catalog inputs use dbt.string_literal, but compiled defining queries are embedded with fixed $pgtrickle$ delimiters and numeric/boolean options are rendered directly, so universal arbitrary-string escaping must not be assumed.

Package change guidance requires execute guards for run_query, result/row checks before indexing, none for missing metadata, focused prefixed wrappers, no Python adapter or dispatch, preservation of hooks/reporting, integration testing, and changelog updates.
The existence, capability, and metadata helpers guard execution and return false/none defaults, but some operations directly iterate results.rows without checking results first.

Single-table refresh qualifies the supplied name, while refresh-all selects graph-managed models using catalog dependency order and has an existence-based fallback for tables not found in its active-table ordering.
Graph-scoped drop only deletes catalog-present stream_table models, whereas force-drop enumerates and drops all catalog stream tables including non-dbt tables.

CDC health checking raises a compiler error for unhealthy returned sources; the status helper classifies drained before paused, errors, staleness, and healthy, returns not_found for missing results, and exposes CDC pause and force-full settings.

The generic stream_table_healthy test directly queries the monitoring view for pause, errors, and staleness; missing catalog entries produce no failing rows and it does not reproduce the helper's drained/CDC-pause classification.
just test-dbt rebuilds the extension E2E image and just test-dbt-fast reuses it; the runner starts a fresh container on default port 15432 and removes it unless keep-container is requested.

The integration runner exercises dependencies, seeds, initial creation, a schedule change from 1m to 3m, repeated runs, full refresh, refresh/freshness operations, and graph-scoped drop; its post-alter assertion is excluded from initial and recreated-state tests.
